autumn: The House comes back. The lawn has been cut for the first time since June and the maples along the drive have started to turn.
A new session, and the first cold morning. Someone has already complained about the heating in the East Block.
September on the Hill: new staff with lanyards, old members with tans, and the trees going early this year.
winter: First morning of the winter sitting. Snow on the lawn, salt on the steps, and the members from the coast arriving in the wrong coats.
Winter. The light is gone by half past four and the office window shows nothing but your own reflection.
December on the Hill. The rink on the canal is open, which the pages talk about, and the supply bill is due, which nobody does.
spring: The thaw. The lawn is brown, the drive is a river, and every member who went south over the break has come back with opinions.
March. The snowbanks on the drive have shrunk to grey ridges and the first tourists are photographing the wrong building.
Spring sitting. Puddles on the steps, the flag snapping in a wet wind, and the budget six weeks out.
summer: June on the Hill. The windows are open, the Speaker has lost patience with the fans, and everyone is counting the days to the rising.
The summer sitting: shirtsleeves in the lobby, a heat haze over the lawn, and the government trying to pass four bills before the House rises.
Summer. The tourists are back on the lawn, the air conditioning is not, and the whip is counting who has already booked flights.

storm: A blizzard. The airport is closed, the drive is a white wall, and the whips on both sides are on the phone to anyone within walking distance.
Snow all night and still falling. The buses are off, the galleries are empty, and Monday's count has a new column: stranded.
The storm of the winter. Plows on the Hill since four, and the member for the farthest riding arriving on foot, triumphant.
firstSnow: First snow of the year, wet and heavy, gone from the pavement by noon and not from the lawn.
The first snow. Light, then not. The pages are delighted; the members with early flights are not.
